argument: Nine text panels must read as one typographic room before they read as a parts inventory. Mixed writing directions, unequal slabs, paper field, and the central pause must carry the composition without interface chrome.

With readout, controls, note, hint, labels, and prose hidden, the first view must leave v040's pressure rack, v041's negative syntax, and v042's hinge body. It should read as a room of reading orientations, not a route diagram, type specimen, or dashboard.

The viewer must stay with one voice rather than connect two mouths or select a gap. Pointer dwell, touch tap, keyboard, and the attend control must expose the same meaningful attention without a hover-only requirement.

A pending dwell must leave the source panel exact. Completion must change actual remote writing-mode, token order, panel bounds, scale, position, and spacing; colour, status, and prose cannot substitute for layout.

The attended panel and its local geometry must remain exact. Two untouched panels elsewhere must answer, proving that attention becomes a relation between reading rooms rather than a local hover effect.
Four remote reflows must compound in the DOM field. Delete must reconstruct the exact preceding layout and release must restore the deterministic quiet room.

Generated DOM text nodes, CSS writing-mode, flex order, panel bounds, and persistent layout state are the medium. No screenshot, imported type specimen, external font, canvas, SVG, or CSS poster may carry the work.

little-critters is translated from situated agents and reciprocal attention into social typography. Animals, eyes, head-turning, characters, paper scene, source palette, source composition, source code, examples, and API surface are refused.

v043 changes medium, composition, encounter, temporal behaviour, shape vocabulary, and viewer task: generated paths and apertures become native DOM text slabs whose reading direction is rewritten by sustained attention elsewhere.

Delete v043 if the blind room is a decorative type poster, if pointer dwell merely highlights a panel, if the source answers itself, if remote layout changes are cosmetic, if touch or keyboard takes a different path, if later reflows reset, or if lifting is inexact.
